body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The top story this morning is a suspicious death on Northrup Street that police are now investigating as a homicide, alongside a DUI checkpoint on Union Avenue that netted two repeat offenders. Outside, it's 73 degrees at Meadows Field with a high near 76 expected, air quality sitting at a moderate 85, and no active weather alerts or fires anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy night across the county, with 30 incidents logged between 7:09 p.m. and 6:44 a.m. Fires led the way with 11 calls, followed by six medical and overdose responses, three crashes and traffic incidents, three disturbances and welfare checks, and two weapons or assault calls.

The evening started early with a fire reported just after 7 p.m., then a pair of medical aids in the 7 and 8 o'clock hours, including one on Oregano Road. Three separate structure fires were logged between 7:59 p.m. and 10:54 p.m., with additional fire calls at 8:54 p.m. and 11:02 p.m. A traffic collision came in at 10:27 p.m., another at 11:32 p.m., and a domestic call and welfare check rounded out the late evening. Deputies also responded to a suspicious person report around 8:31 p.m. and an officer assist at 8:09 p.m.

After midnight, the pace didn't let up. A welfare call came in on Taft Highway just past midnight, followed by an outside fire on West Niles Street at 12:25 a.m. and more fire calls at 12:29 a.m. and 2 a.m., the latter a vehicle fire. Two shootings were reported — one at 1:29 a.m. and another at 5:58 a.m. — and a warrant service and probation check were both logged at 3:12 a.m. A fire on Jefferson Street came in at 3:55 a.m., with medical aids following at 4:04 a.m. and 4:05 a.m. on Wilson Road. The final call of the night was a traffic collision at 6:40 a.m., just as the morning commute was getting started. All details remain preliminary until confirmed by an official source.

## Today's weather

It's a mild November morning in Bakersfield, with the current observation at Meadows Field reading 73 degrees. Today's high should top out near 76, and tonight's low will settle around 52 — comfortable sweater weather, nothing more. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no fires burning in the area. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 85, which is fine for most folks, though those with sensitive respiratory conditions may want to keep an eye on it if they're planning extended time outdoors. All in all, a good day to be outside.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police arrested two drivers with previous DUI convictions during a checkpoint on Union Avenue.** The operation was aimed at catching impaired drivers before they could hurt someone, and the fact that both arrests involved people who had already been convicted of DUI before is a sobering reminder of how persistent the problem can be. Checkpoints like this one are a regular tool local law enforcement uses to keep the roads safer, and this weekend's results show why they keep doing them.

**According to KGET 17, the death of a man found in a vacant lot on Northrup Street is being treated as suspicious by Bakersfield police.** Investigators have not released many details yet, but the circumstances surrounding the discovery prompted detectives to take a closer look. Bakersfield Now reports that the department is now investigating the case as a homicide, which means the investigation has shifted into a more serious phase. Anyone with information is encouraged to reach out to the Bakersfield Police Department.

**KGET 17 also tells us that trial has begun in the case of a Bakersfield crash that killed two sisters who were delivering newspapers.** The crash took the lives of two women who were simply doing their early-morning route, a loss that hit the community hard when it happened. Now the case is moving through the courts, and the trial will determine accountability for a tragedy that left a family and a neighborhood grieving. We'll be watching as the proceedings continue.

**23ABC reports that California voters have rejected Proposition 41, according to the Associated Press.** The measure would have added new rules for special taxes proposed in the state, including requiring a state audit before certain tax measures could go before voters. It also would have prevented state taxes approved after January 1, 2026, from keeping revenue they generate outside California's voter-approved spending limit, and taxes that didn't follow that requirement would have been invalidated. Programs receiving money from new state special taxes would have faced audits before an election and on a recurring basis. The measure's defeat means the existing rules for special taxes remain in place for now.

**Bakersfield Now reports on a historic first hanging on Mississippi's razor-close Senate count.** While that story is far from Kern County, it's one of those national political moments that could shape the balance of power in Washington, and it's worth keeping an eye on as the count continues. We'll have more if it develops.

## Something good

**23ABC brought us a wonderful story out of Memorial Stadium this weekend, where Bakersfield College celebrated the 50th anniversary of its 1976 Junior Rose Bowl championship.** Some of those same players from five decades ago returned to the field, including Michael Georgino, who said walking back into the stadium felt like yesterday. The Renegades capped the night with a 40-21 win over College of the Canyons, finishing the regular season on a four-game winning streak and a 6-4 record. The team is expected to play in a bowl game for the first time since 2024 — a fitting way to honor a legacy that still means something in this town.

## Coming up this week

The City of Bakersfield has a couple of public meetings on the calendar today. The Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m., and the Youth Commission gathers at 4:30 p.m. Both are open to the public, and if you've got something on your mind about how the city runs its fire department or its youth programs, these are the rooms to be in.

Looking further out, the Fox Theater has a full slate of events lined up. Tonight, the Cults & Classics series presents "Play Misty for Me" — a chance to see the Clint Eastwood thriller on the big screen. On Friday, November 13, the NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet takes the stage, a holiday tradition that always draws a crowd. The 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards follows on Sunday, November 15, celebrating two decades of local country talent. And if you're already thinking ahead to Thanksgiving weekend, Becky Robinson's Holiday Spectacular arrives on November 27, with "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" rounding out the Cults & Classics series on November 23. Tickets are available through the Fox Theater box office.

That's your Monday morning, Bakersfield. Have a good one, and we'll see you back here tomorrow.

top.title: 2 drivers with previous convictions arrested for DUI during checkpoint on Union Ave: Bakersfield PD
